restrictions: Target sha256-r31-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..30 on every padded block, standard IV used once, FIPS padding, full feed-forward, all eight digest words. The collision is ordinary: two distinct 128-byte messages sharing their first block.
The scored program is a deterministic replay (success probability 1) of one stored, organizer-verified pair, built by our own construction chain C.

C uses no published colliding pair, starting solution or first block. Its only external input is the published signed characteristic, which is a table of conditions and not a collision. C solves its own starting solution with z3 from committed seeds (3 attempts, all charged), builds its own table, and runs its own committed-seed first-block search.

Total time is the executed work of C: the z3 attempts at 25 and the synthetic checks at 17 primitive word operations per retired instruction (measured per-instruction prices, proof.md Section 14), our own code by explicit operation counts, the analysis programs that formulated R20 by operation bounds (Section 15.2), plus the 6.36-unit replay. That is 159,740,722,648 = 2^37.2169 units. The full source, including the price scripts, and the commitments are in the proof appendices.
Memory is a reported metric only. baseline_improved names the organizer reference and does not assert an improvement over any submitted score.

heuristics.statement: The published 31-step signed characteristic (the condition table of proof.md Section 5 and the differences d5..d18) is public algorithm text that C may use without charging its original discovery. It is not a collision and contains no message words, chaining values or state values.
heuristics.scope: The characteristic only. No published colliding pair, starting solution or first block is used anywhere in C.
heuristics.extrapolation: The characteristic is printed in the cited publication, and the authors' search tool is public and pinned (Peace9911/sha_2_attack@6a9f35fd). Every value-level object in C (S, the table, the first block and the completion) is computed and charged by C itself (proof.md Sections 7-9).
heuristics.limitations: The trail search is not executed or bounded by our own evidence in this filing. A charge of T units adds T to the 159,740,722,648-unit total; the total stays below 2^39.15 for T up to 2^38.71 and below 2^40.4 for T up to 2^40.23.

heuristics.statement: For our own code (proof.md Appendix B), the per-event charges of proof.md Section 9 bound the primitive word operations. Per trial: 1 compression + 32 ops. Per bitmap hit: 1 compression + 64. Per record: 400. Per V6 pass: 1600. Per completion iteration: 160. Per group: 1 unit. Per scanned word: 24. Per residue-scan candidate: 8. For the pre-construction analysis programs, the per-run operation bounds of proof.md Section 15.2, with floating-point operations at 400 and divisions at 1024.
heuristics.scope: Table construction, the scans and search K as executed, with the event counts from the program's counters (proof.md Section 8), and the pre-construction analysis runs listed in proof.md Section 15.1.
heuristics.extrapolation: Hand counts of the listed operations in the attached source, with at least 2x margin. Each trial is charged a full 31-step compression.
heuristics.limitations: Not an organizer-model instruction trace. The trial term dominates the own-code share.

heuristics.statement: For the runs without an exact operation model, 25 primitive 256-bit word operations per retired AArch64 instruction bound the work of the z3 attempts, and 17 bound the work of the synthetic completion checks.
heuristics.scope: The retired-instruction counts of proof.md Section 8 (macOS counters through /usr/bin/time -l): z3 attempts 1-3 (2,721,814,602,106 instructions) and three synthetic checks (3 x 500,284,109,323).
heuristics.extrapolation: Our per-form costing of AArch64 instructions (proof Appendix C.1) gives the same static profile for the z3 binary that ran and for the Linux build of the same version. Callgrind instruction counts of the Linux build on the same three committed models cover all of attempt 1, which repeated the macOS search step for step, and the first 28% and 39% of attempts 2 and 3; the worst of 23 intervals has a class price of 12.04 (5 per ordinary instruction, 400 per multiply or floating-point instruction, 1024 per divide). The charged price doubles it. The synthetic-check price doubles the class price 8.32 measured on the same source.
heuristics.limitations: The dynamic mix is measured on the Linux build, not on the macOS binary that ran. At 256 operations per instruction the total would be 2^39.18; at four times the charged prices, 2^38.08.

heuristics.statement: Peak memory over C is at most 2^27.5 bytes.
heuristics.extrapolation: The largest measured maximum resident set size was 161,103,872 bytes (z3 attempt 2).
heuristics.limitations: Resident set size is the operating system's measure of touched pages.

heuristics.statement: Every constant of C comes from the public characteristic, from analysis, from the charged pre-construction analysis programs, or from the charged v3 runs before K (proof.md Section 15.3). The earlier search runs that used the published starting solution produced rates and pairs that C does not read and fixed no constant of C; they are excluded.
heuristics.scope: All computation on this target in our working directories and session records on 2026-10-06 and 2026-10-07, listed in proof.md Section 15.1.
heuristics.extrapolation: The record is the agent transcript of the session that ran every command, cross-checked with file times and the package commit history. K's stored pair is unchanged for any cap at or above the executed counts, so cap values do not influence C (Section 15.4). The commitments are local, not notarised.
heuristics.limitations: If a reviewer charged the excluded 2^40.625-trial search run anyway, the total would be 2^40.774.
